questions.q: What are the two layers of every expense report in Oracle Fusion Expenses?
options: The report header and the expense items
The approval queue and the payment file
The chart of accounts and the ledger
The corporate card and the bank statement
questions.explain: A report consists of a header (purpose, template, business unit) and one or more expense items, each with its own type, date, and amount.

questions.q: What are the two ways an expense item can be added to a report?
options: Manual entry, or starting from an imported corporate card transaction
Only by calling the Payables help desk
Only by uploading a spreadsheet
Only through the mobile app, never on the web
questions.explain: Items are added either by manual entry or by confirming an imported transaction from a corporate card issuer feed.

questions.q: Why do most companies encourage using imported corporate card transactions when a card was used?
options: Because manual entry is against company policy everywhere
Because the amount, date, and merchant are already accurate from the card network and can't be mistyped
Because imported transactions skip all audit rules
Because imported transactions are always reimbursed faster
questions.explain: Importing from the card feed avoids manual data entry errors since the transaction data comes directly from the card network.

questions.q: When does Oracle Fusion Expenses run policy checks and audit rules against an expense report?
options: Continuously the moment each item is typed, before the report even exists
Only when the employee saves a draft
At submission, when every applicable rule runs across every item on the report at once
Only after the report has already been reimbursed
questions.explain: Nothing is validated against policy or routed for approval until the employee clicks Submit, at which point all items are checked together.

questions.q: Why can a report with nine normal items and one over-policy item still get flagged as a whole?
options: Because Oracle always flags every report regardless of content
Because audit and policy evaluation applies at the report level once any item triggers a rule
Because the nine normal items are automatically deleted
Because reports can only contain a single item
questions.explain: Audit rule evaluation and routing happen at the report level, so one problematic item is enough to flag the entire report for review.
